newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - Aug 15.

text.p: No win, Win: New Zealand First leader and Treasurer Winston Peters suffered his greatest blow in politics when wine-box commissioner Sir Ronald Davison threw out his allegations of fraud and conspiracy. Page 1.
Banking lags overseas trend: New Zealand banking is ignoring an international trend for banks and their competitors to collaborate. Page 1.
Power play rumbles under Waikato farmland: A nominee company is set to reveal its plans to to exploit a valuable energy resource in rural Waikato. Page 1.
Big compliance costs in savings tax regime: Superannuation and life fund managers face major adminstrative and compliance costs under a new savings tax regime proposed this week. Page 2.
Cronyism fear in MMP aftermath: MMP could foster political cronyism, Higher Salaries commissioner Hutton Peacock said. Page 2.

Art deco wharf building for apartment complex: Retailers could be moving into new sites on Auckland's Princes Wharf as early as the middle of next year, with serviced apartments expected to go on sale on October this year. Page 4.

Russians wait with open arms for NZ produce: There was good news for New Zealand food exporters this week -- the Russian market of 150 million consumers has a growing appetite for imports and plenty of money to pay for them. Page 12.
MetService has been warned by the Commerce Commission to play fair with competitors or face prosecution. Page 13.
Apple industry moves to defuse timebomb: The apple industry is facing a crisis and for the first time the Apple and Pear Marketing Board is admitting it. Page 15.

Win rebuts winebox whitewasher: Treasurer Winston Peters and his lawyer Brian Henry will ask the Court of Appeal to rule on whether an interpretation of tax law at the heart of winebox commissioner Sir Ron Davison's report is correct. Page 1.

Accountants encroach on lawyers' patch: Big Six accounting firm KPMG is planning to set up a law firm in Auckland, parallel to its accounting, human resources and information technology operations. Page 1.

Have we too many fish in the aquarium market?: Investors are bailing out of listed aquarium developer Richina Pacific and putting their money with new aquarium rival, Queen Charlotte Holdings. Page 3.

Court rules against gov't drug buying agency: A decision by the government drugs buying agency Pharmac to halve the subsidy on the frequently prescribed drug Rulide has been overturned by the High Court. Page 3.
Tax credits in sight for small investors: Relief is in sight for low and middle-income New Zealanders paying too much tax on their superannuation and insurance investments. Page 4.

Clocked car crusader's case stalled: A move by clocked car crusader Dermot Nottingham to have a bankruptcy proceeding against him thrown out has been delayed after documents were filed late in the High Court at Auckland. Page 4.
